hints.title: Bivariate Monotonic Saddle Search
hints.text: Because f(x, y) is strictly increasing with respect to both variables, the search space resembles a sorted 2D matrix.

hints.title: Two Pointers from Opposing Extremes
hints.text: Initialize x at 1 and y at 1000. If f(x, y) is greater than z, decrease y; if less than z, increase x.

hints.title: Two Pointers Search Blueprint
hints.text: While x <= 1000 and y >= 1: evaluate val = customfunction.f(x, y). If val == z: record [x, y], x++, y--. Else adjust x or y.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Each comparison step increments x or decrements y, totaling at most 2000 evaluations.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all pairs (x, y) takes O(X * Y) = 1,000,000 function evaluations.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Exploiting monotonicity reduces search boundary to linear frontier traversal.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Two-pointer matrix saddleback search rather than nested loops.
